summary: Ran full backend regression (36 pytest tests, all pass) and end-to-end UI walkthrough on CyberHead Academy. Backend APIs, auth (JWT + httpOnly cookie), courses (8 seeded, filter, search, slug/id lookup, enroll idempotency), student dashboard (progresses 31/48/72), profile update, contact form, admin RBAC (401 unauth, 403 non-admin), rate limiting on login, Security Lab classification (SQLi/XSS/CMD/PATH), request-log middleware and stats all working. Found one critical routing bug: the frontend React route '/api/docs' collides with the backend '/api/*' ingress, so the API Docs page is unreachable (navbar link returns raw JSON 404 from FastAPI). Everything else UI-wise (Home, Courses, Course details w/ curriculum, Search, Login/Register/Dashboard/Profile, Security Lab + WAF dashboard, Contact, 404) works correctly.

minor.issue: Unmatched routes return FastAPI default {"detail":"Not Found"} instead of the standard {success:false,error:{code,message}} envelope defined by the HTTPException handler. Add a StarletteHTTPException / catch-all 404 handler for consistency.

ui_bugs.issue: Route path '/api/docs' collides with backend ingress rule (all /api/* routes go to FastAPI). Navigating to /api/docs from navbar 'API Docs' link or footer returns raw JSON {"detail":"Not Found"} from the backend; the ApiDocs React page is never mounted.

action_items: Rename frontend route '/api/docs' to something outside the /api/* namespace (e.g. '/docs' or '/api-docs'). Update: /app/frontend/src/App.js, /app/frontend/src/components/Navbar.jsx (nav-apidocs-link), /app/frontend/src/components/Footer.jsx.
(Nice-to-have) Register a Starlette 404 handler that returns the same {success:false, error:{code:'NOT_FOUND', message:'...'}} envelope so unknown /api paths are consistent with app errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Route collision: any frontend route that starts with '/api' will be shadowed by the backend ingress. Keep the SPA namespace fully outside '/api'.
Global exception handler only wraps HTTPException — Starlette-raised 404s (unmatched routes, method not allowed) bypass it and leak FastAPI defaults.
get_current_user reads token from cookie OR Authorization header; consistent with client that stores 'ch_token' in localStorage and also receives httpOnly cookie — good.
bcrypt is used correctly, hashes are $2b$ format; admin seed is idempotent and re-hashes when ADMIN_PASSWORD changes — matches playbook.
Rate limiting is in-memory (per-process) — acceptable for demo; note it will reset on backend reload and won't work across multiple workers.

CORS uses allow_credentials=True with allow_origins '*' via env default. In production this combination is invalid per CORS spec (browsers reject credentialed requests with wildcard origins). CORS_ORIGINS env should be a specific origin in prod.

Once E1 renames the /api/docs frontend route, re-verify by navigating to the new URL, clicking 'API Docs' in navbar+footer, and confirming ApiDocs page renders with 'Authentication' group. Also verify the swagger-link still opens /api/swagger. Dashboard route is '/security-lab/dashboard' (not '/security-lab-dashboard'). Logout is inside Navbar user dropdown with data-testid='menu-logout' (not 'logout-button').
rca of the issue: The React SPA registers Route path='/api/docs'. In this environment, the Kubernetes ingress unconditionally routes any URL prefixed with '/api' to the FastAPI service on port 8001. Because '/api/docs' matches the ingress rule before it can be handled by the frontend, the request hits FastAPI, which has no such route registered (docs are served at /api/swagger), so it returns the default 404 JSON. Fix: rename the frontend route to a path outside the '/api' namespace (e.g. '/docs' or '/api-docs') and update the two links in Navbar.jsx and Footer.jsx accordingly.
